_ghi_chu: Rà soát 2026-11-21 — bản phủ tiếng Anh cho công cụ Cửa – Chủ – Bếp (ban biên tập viết, chờ người bản xứ duyệt). Lời sách xưa (nha / bep / minh_kinh) chỉ có bản Việt.

thuan.cua_chu: The entrance and the main resting room support each other: the home feels easy to settle into and daily routines hold.
thuan.cua_bep: The stove sits well with the entrance: cooking flows easily and family meals are easier to keep regular.
thuan.chu_bep: Stove and main room suit each other: the person cooking and the person resting rarely get in each other's way.

can_bang.cua_chu: Door and main room share the same direction of energy: steady, nothing added or taken away.
can_bang.cua_bep: The stove is neutral relative to the door: keep the kitchen clean and airy and it works well.
can_bang.chu_bep: Stove and main room are on equal terms: nothing to adjust.

can_chu_dong.cua_chu: By this book, the door and the main room do not support each other: look after quiet and sleep in the main room, and choose a supportive side for the stove to rebalance.
can_chu_dong.cua_bep: By this book, the stove does not yet suit the door: keep the kitchen dry, bright and tidy; when you next renovate, consider a better-suited side.
can_chu_dong.chu_bep: By this book, the stove and the main room do not suit each other: keep cooking smells and heat out of the main room (a closed door, an extractor fan).

ket_luan.thuan: Door, main room and stove all support each other — by this book, a well-balanced home.
ket_luan.can_bang: Some pairs suit each other, some do not — the home works fine with a few small adjustments.
ket_luan.can_chu_dong: The door and main room do not support each other and the stove does not rebalance them — start with the stove position and how the main room is used.

cung_nhom.co: All three sit in the same group (East group or West group).
cung_nhom.khong: The three are not all in the same East / West group.

viec.hop: The stove is already on a supportive side: keep it there and keep the kitchen dry and bright.
viec.xoay: Free: turn the stove so the cook faces {huong}.
viec.doi: When you next renovate the kitchen: consider moving the stove to the {huong} side — it suits both the door and the main room.
viec.doi_cua: When you next renovate the kitchen: consider moving the stove to the {huong} side — it suits the main door.
viec.giu: Free: keep a door between kitchen and main room and run the extractor while cooking.

can_cu.sach_khac: Another classic (Ten Books on Dwellings) advises the opposite — set the stove on a weaker side with its mouth facing a good direction. These are two different readings; we do not choose for you.

cong_cu.luu_y_tham_khao: These notes summarise classical texts named in each item and are for cultural reference only. cong_cu.nhom_c_an: The book has {n} more strongly worded notes about this layout — shown only to readers aged 16 or over.
cong_cu.viec_tuan_tieu_de: The stove sits on a side the Yangzhai Sanyao advises against

nhieu_lop.tieu_de: Multi-courtyard homes: the star on the main building

tinh.y: One courtyard, one row of buildings: the book reads Door – Main room – Stove as above and does not count stars by row.

dong.y: Two to five rows: the book counts stars from the gate inwards; each row's star is produced by the element of the row before. Read the star of the row where the main (tallest) building stands.

bien.y: Six to ten rows: counted like a moving house, but Metal, Wood and Earth may come in pairs — two stars of the same element side by side.

hoa.y: Eleven rows or more: the book counts with the He Tu and Luo Shu numbers. Hieuban does not calculate this yet.

quan_he.ty_hoa: same element as the main building's side
quan_he.cung_sinh_sao: fed by the main building's side
quan_he.sao_khac_cung: clashing with the main building's side
quan_he.cung_khac_sao: held down by the main building's side

lop_chu.thuan: The main building, in row {so}, gets the star {sao} ({du_nien}), {quan_he}. The book sees this as favourable: a good star in the right place.
lop_chu.can_bang: The main building, in row {so}, gets the star {sao} ({du_nien}), {quan_he}. One side favourable, one side not — the book treats it as ordinary.
lop_chu.can_chu_dong: The main building, in row {so}, gets the star {sao} ({du_nien}), {quan_he}. Worth attention: the book suggests moving the height and main living space to a row with a better star when you next renovate.

nhieu_lop.chua_lop_chu: Choose the row with the main (tallest, largest) building to see which star falls on it.
nhieu_lop.nen_cao: Rows that suit the main building (good star, element in harmony with its side): {ds}.
nhieu_lop.khong_nen_cao: No row has both a good star and an element in harmony with the main building's side — keep the main building as it is and mind the Door – Main room – Stove pairs above.
nhieu_lop.ap_sat: The door and the main building do not suit each other, but a good star falls on the main building. The book calls this a good star holding the clash down: the early years are often smooth, and the door–main clash shows only over time. Worth fixing the door–main pair gradually (entrance, main room) when you can.
nhieu_lop.quy_uoc: Hieuban's convention (the book was written for old multi-courtyard houses, not today's townhouses): row 1 is the gate or front door; each further building with its own roof, separated by a courtyard or light well, adds one row. A house under one roof with no inner courtyard is a still house.
nhieu_lop.cua_lech: Gate set to one side: the first row's star is counted from the gate's side.
nhieu_lop.bay_lop: Seven-row house: the book only gives an example for row 6; the pairing at row 7 follows the book's rule (seven rows pair two elements).

can_cu.dau: Row 1 (gate): the you nian from the {tu} side to the facing side {huong} is {du_nien}.
can_cu.luat_dong: Moving house: each row's star is produced by the element of the row before (Earth → Metal → Water → Wood → Fire → Earth), one star per element.
can_cu.luat_bien: Changing house: Metal, Wood and Earth come in pairs (Fu Bi – Tan Lang, Lu Cun – Ju Men, Wu Qu – Po Jun); six rows pair one element, seven two, eight or more all three.

lech.ap_dung: Where you stood, the compass was off by {do}° from the house axis; every reading inside has been corrected by that amount.
lech.nhieu: Strong magnetic interference where you stood ({do}° off the house axis): step away from the fridge, induction hob or steel frame and measure the axis again, or use the scaled floor outline.
lech.chua_truc: The house axis has not been measured, so indoor interference is not corrected. Lay the edge of your phone along a long wall for a firmer result.
lech.chua_huong: No front-door direction yet, so the house axis cannot be checked; readings are used as the compass gave them.

canh_bao.chua_on_dinh: The compass needle was moving while you measured — hold the phone still and point again.
canh_bao.sat_ranh_8: Right on the line between {a} and {b}: step half a metre aside and point again, or read both sides.
canh_bao.sat_ranh_son: Right on the line between two mountains — the mountain name is uncertain.

vi_tri.cua_tang: On an upper floor, the top of the stairs leading up to it is taken as that floor's “door” — a common modern practice, not yet checked against the classical texts.
vi_tri.chua_du: This floor needs a door (ground floor: main door · upper floor: top of the stairs) and at least the main room or the stove to check door, room and stove.

ten_cap_tren.cua_chu: Top of the stairs and main room
ten_cap_tren.cua_bep: Top of the stairs and stove
